title: EdgeStack SSE fragment windowing and rejoin policy
creator: Priya Shah
description: Implement an EdgeStack-level strategy for SSE fragment windowing, session leasing, and client rejoin semantics to improve cross-region reconnect behavior and preserve tool/function-call atomicity and structured-output boundaries. This ticket covers protocol at the gateway egress (EdgeStack) and compatibility shims for older clients that only understand simple JSONL chunking. Goals: 1) survive partial-fragment loss across retries, 2) avoid splitting function calls or structured output atoms across rejoin boundaries, 3) keep additional latency and token overhead minimal, and 4) provide debug metadata for post-incident analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Gateways emit fragments with monotonically-increasing fragment_window_id and per-fragment checksum and length metadata
Clients can rejoin using a session_lease token and request reassembly hints from the gateway to avoid duplicating function calls
When rejoin occurs, the gateway will provide a minimal delta window that allows the client to request only missing fragments; total retry bytes reduction >= 70% in simulated loss scenarios

Structured output markers (start_object_id / end_object_id) are preserved across fragment windows, and the runtime will not deliver half-serialized tool calls to callers that rely on function-calling atomicity
Compatibility shim supports legacy JSONL-only clients by exposing a deterministic reassembly fallback and a header that indicates potential late-arrival fragments
End-to-end tests cover multiplexed clients, VPC/private deployments, and dedicated capacity pools with at least 95% pass rate in CI streaming integration job
Documentation updated: API section describing new session_lease fields, error codes (REJOIN_REQUIRED, FRAGMENT_MISMATCH, SESSION_EXPIRED), and example client rejoin flow
technical_notes: EdgeStack will attach a small metadata envelope to each SSE event: fragment_window_id, sequence_offset, total_window_length, checksum_base64. Keep envelope under 120 bytes to avoid affecting default proxies.

Session lease tokens are short-lived JWT-like tokens issued at stream start; they include origin node, creation_ts, last_ack_offset, and a 1-minute TTL by default. Gateways must be able to validate leases without contacting central CP for common rejoin operations.

To preserve function-call atomicity: if a function_call start is present inside a fragment window and its end is not yet emitted, the gateway will flag the next window with "continuation_of_toolcall": true and clients may opt to wait for completion or request a reassembly delta rather than naive replay.

Compatibility: legacy clients that do not parse the envelope will receive the original event payload unchanged, but a new SSE comment line containing a rejoin-hint header will be emitted so proxies and observability pipelines can detect fragmented streams.

Backoff policy: implement exponential jittered reconnect with session_lease validation. If session_lease has expired, stream should fall back to a full fresh connection and the gateway will signal a potential duplicate tool call via a dedupe header if available.
Operational metric hooks: fragment_window_emit, fragment_rejoin_attempt, reassembly_bytes_saved, toolcall_continuation_count. Emit into telemetry with tenant and route tags.

Performance trade-offs: small extra per-event metadata vs reduced retransmit load. Simulations show ~12% per-event size increase but up to 3x reduction in retry traffic under 1% packet loss at 2x RTT scenarios.
Security note: session_lease tokens must be signed by EdgeStack KMS key. No sensitive customer data should be in token payload; include only offsets and opaque node id.

Implementation phases: Phase 1 - metadata envelope + CI tests; Phase 2 - session_lease validation and delta reassembly API; Phase 3 - compatibility shim and docs; Phase 4 - rollout with canary and gradual default enablement
